solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Across dale, up top, ruined with too many souls (13)

indicatorNotes.ruined: ruined letters are wrecked and rearranged

blocks.note: across = over, as in 'over the river'
the nine letters of DALE UP TOP, rearranged

annotation.surface: A walker complains that a once-quiet dale, and the hilltop above it, has been spoiled by crowds.
annotation.walkthrough: The comma after 'dale' is there only for the surface; 'dale, up top' is one run of fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: An overpopulated place holds too many people, and 'souls' is an old word for people.

entries.clue: What may enhance bite of hot tandoori potentially? (11)

indicatorNotes.potentially: the letters could potentially become something else

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 11 letters

annotation.surface: A diner wonders whether a hot tandoori dish might make a meal bite harder.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bite' sounds like the kick of a spicy dish; it is the way the teeth meet, which orthodontists correct.
annotation.definitionFit: Orthodontia is dental work that straightens teeth and so improves the bite.

entries.clue: Torture encountered in French and African land (5)

indicatorNotes.encountered in: GYP is met inside the French word

blocks.note: et is French for 'and'
gyp = pain, torment, as in 'my knee is giving me gyp'

annotation.surface: A report of torture found in a French-speaking African country.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Gyp' is British informal for pain or torment, so 'torture' stretches it only a little.
annotation.definitionFit: Egypt is a country in north Africa.

entries.clue: Contemporaries look mature renouncing whiskey (4,5)

indicatorNotes.renouncing: the word gives up, so loses, the W

blocks.note: to peer = to look closely
GROW UP (mature) without W, whiskey in the phonetic alphabet

annotation.surface: Advice that people of one's age look more grown-up once they give up whisky.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Whiskey' is only the letter W, and 'mature' is the phrasal verb GROW UP rather than an adjective.
annotation.definitionFit: Your peer group is the people of your own age and standing: your contemporaries.

entries.clue: Issue favouring millennials? (7)

blocks.note: pro = in favour of
Gen Y = the millennial generation

annotation.surface: A political question that favours young voters.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Issue' reads as a political topic; here it means offspring, and the question mark flags the loose use of Gen Y.
annotation.definitionFit: Issue in the legal sense is children or descendants, which is what progeny means.

entries.clue: Celebrate American motor racing legend (5)

blocks.note: to laud = to praise
A = American

annotation.surface: A call to honour an American racing driver.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes the legend American; Niki Lauda was an Austrian Formula One champion.
annotation.definitionFit: Niki Lauda was a three-times Formula One world champion.

entries.clue: Terriers outside listen to barking Spanish visitors (3,6)

indicatorNotes.outside: TA sits outside the other pieces

blocks.note: the Territorial Army, whose soldiers are nicknamed Terriers; it wraps the rest
hear = listen
barking (mad) = crazy

annotation.surface: Dogs outside hear the barking of Spanish tourists.
annotation.walkthrough: Terriers and barking make a dog scene; the Territorial Army is the British part-time reserve, and 'barking' is British slang for mad.
annotation.definitionFit: The Spanish Armada sailed to England in 1588: unwelcome Spanish visitors.

entries.clue: Fox turned up very small object (3)

indicatorNotes.turned up: in a down clue, turned up means read from bottom to top

blocks.note: tod is an old word for a fox

annotation.surface: A fox appears as a tiny speck in the distance.
annotation.walkthrough: Tod is an old country word for a fox, rarely met outside crosswords.
annotation.definitionFit: A dot is a tiny spot or speck.

entries.clue: Pet lost having run out for stick (4)

indicatorNotes.out: the R goes out of the word

blocks.note: a stray is a lost pet
R = run, as in cricket scoring, removed

annotation.surface: A lost dog has run off to fetch a stick.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stick' is the verb, as in 'stick around', not the thing a dog fetches.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: stick in the sense of remaining put, as in 'stick around'.

entries.clue: Profits from light unit used in online vehicle tests? (10)

indicatorNotes.used in: something used in a machine is fitted inside it, so the light unit goes inside the tests

blocks.note: E (electronic, online) + MOTS, Britain's annual roadworthiness tests
the lumen is the unit of luminous flux

annotation.surface: Someone earns money from a lighting device used in online car inspections.
annotation.walkthrough: An MOT is the yearly test a British car must pass; the question mark admits online MOTs are fanciful.
annotation.definitionFit: Emoluments are earnings from a job, a formal word for profits or pay.

entries.clue: Warring Veronese house united in cinematic scene (8)

indicatorNotes.in: united in a scene means placed inside it, so U sits within the film word

blocks.note: a montage is a film sequence of cut shots
U = united, as in football club names

annotation.surface: A film shows the feuding family from Verona brought together in one scene.
annotation.walkthrough: 'United' plays against 'warring' in the surface; the Montagues fight the Capulets in Romeo and Juliet.
annotation.definitionFit: The Montagues are Romeo's family, at war with the Capulets in Verona.

entries.clue: Marketing division going nowhere? (6)

blocks.note: ad = advertisement, marketing
a rift is a split or division

annotation.surface: A company's marketing department is stalled.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Marketing division' reads as one department; it is two pieces. The question mark covers adrift, which drifts rather than stays put.
annotation.definitionFit: Something adrift has lost its way, so is getting nowhere.

entries.clue: Rebellious figure’s claim keeping relative in Florida (6,5)

indicatorNotes.in: someone kept in Florida is located within it, so the pieces sit inside the state's letters

blocks.note: FL is the postal code for Florida
to allege = to claim
nan = grandmother

annotation.surface: A rebel's lawsuit tries to keep a relative in Florida.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is'. Two containers nest: NAN inside ALLEGE, then that inside FL.
annotation.definitionFit: A fallen angel, like Lucifer, is one cast out of heaven for rebelling against God.

entries.clue: Rather fatty steak may not be so well done (4,3,3)

annotation.definition2: Rather fatty steak may not be so

blocks.clueFragment: Rather fatty steak may not be so
blocks.note: the stock health warning about fatty meat
a cry of congratulation, not a cooking instruction

annotation.surface: A cook warns that a fatty steak may not be cooked through.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Well done' looks like a steak order; it is the praise 'good for you!', and fatty steak is also not good for you.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Good for you!' is said to praise someone, and fatty food is not healthy, so both senses fit.

entries.clue: Round near ground make hasty exit (2,1,6)

indicatorNotes.ground: ground up, the letters are broken and remixed

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

annotation.surface: A boxer near the end of a round on home ground decides to flee.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ground' looks like a place, a sports ground; it is the past tense of grind. To do a runner is British slang for leaving in a hurry, often without paying.
annotation.definitionFit: Doing a runner means running off quickly, usually to dodge a bill.

entries.clue: Leading crossword compilers disturbing people (9)

blocks.note: up = ahead, leading, as in 'two goals up'
setters write crosswords

annotation.surface: Top crossword setters are said to trouble their solvers.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Leading crossword compilers' reads as one phrase about the best setters; 'leading' is its own piece.
annotation.definitionFit: Upsetters are people who disturb or upset others.

entries.clue: Turner’s beer with ten consumed (4)

indicatorNotes.consumed: the ale consumes, so holds, the X

blocks.note: ale is beer
X is ten in Roman numerals

annotation.surface: The painter Turner drinks beer with ten others.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital T makes 'Turner' look like the painter J.M.W. Turner; it is anything that turns.
annotation.definitionFit: An axle is the rod a wheel turns on, so a turner.

entries.clue: Walk under cover from Athens to Alexandria (4)

indicatorNotes.from: the answer comes from within the words that follow

blocks.note: the last letter of Athens, the whole of 'to', and the first of Alexandria

annotation.surface: A traveller walks in secret from Athens to Alexandria.
annotation.walkthrough: The Greek place names suit the answer, a Greek colonnade.
annotation.definitionFit: A stoa is a covered walkway or portico in ancient Greece.

entries.clue: Sherpa provoked and mimicked hippy? (4-6)

indicatorNotes.provoked: stirred up, so the letters are shaken into a new order

blocks.note: the six letters of SHERPA, rearranged
to ape = to copy

annotation.surface: A Himalayan guide was goaded and copied a hippie.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hippy' looks like a flower child; it means broad in the hips, and the question mark flags the definition by example.
annotation.definitionFit: A pear-shaped figure is widest at the hips.

entries.clue: Bacteria perhaps in A&E gowns (7)

blocks.note: A&E is the British hospital emergency department
robes = gowns

annotation.surface: Germs may lurk on the hospital gowns in the emergency department.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' is there because not all aerobes are bacteria.
annotation.definitionFit: Aerobes are organisms, often bacteria, that need oxygen to live.

entries.clue: Copper guarding university interrupts 5am clean (6)

indicatorNotes.guarding: CU guards U by standing round it
indicatorNotes.interrupts: what interrupts something breaks into the middle of it, so these letters split VA from M

blocks.note: V is five in Roman numerals, then AM
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
U = university

annotation.surface: A police officer on a campus beat breaks up a 5am cleaning session.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Copper' is a policeman in the surface and the metal in the wordplay; '5am' looks like a time but splits into a Roman numeral and AM.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain verb synonym: cleaning a carpet with a suction cleaner takes its name from the machine.

entries.clue: Low comment about certain races in recurring phrase (5)

indicatorNotes.about: a comment about a subject goes round it, so the cow's noise goes around the races

blocks.note: cattle low, and what they say is 'moo'
the TT races are the Isle of Man motorcycle races

annotation.surface: A mean remark about particular races in a phrase that keeps coming back.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Low' reads as base or mean; it is the noise a cow makes.
annotation.definitionFit: A motto is a phrase used again and again as a rule or slogan.

entries.clue: Speech dropping intro, a line endowed with reason (8)

indicatorNotes.dropping intro: the word drops its first letter

blocks.note: ORATION (speech) without its first letter
as printed
L = line

annotation.surface: A speaker cuts the opening of a speech and gives a sensible line.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Intro' means the first letter only, so ORATION loses just its O.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a rational being can think logically, which is what being endowed with reason means.

entries.clue: Old rambler sheepish indeed! (5)

blocks.note: O = old
a rambler is a climbing plant, like a vine
surface padding: an exclamation stressing that 'sheepish' is meant literally

annotation.surface: An old hiker looking embarrassed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rambler' sounds like a walker and 'sheepish' like shy; both are taken literally. 'Indeed!' says the definition is exact: ovine is sheep-like to the letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Ovine means of or like sheep: literally sheepish.

entries.clue: Approximate data in list equals set here? (5,5)

blocks.note: round figures are approximate
a table lists data

annotation.surface: A statistician asks whether rough data in a list forms a set of equal values.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Equals' and 'set' sound like maths; they are peers who sat at King Arthur's Round Table, which had no head so that none ranked higher.
annotation.definitionFit: The Round Table seated Arthur's knights as equals, and the question mark flags the cryptic hint.

entries.clue: Plump from zero exercise (3)

blocks.note: O looks like zero
PT = physical training

annotation.surface: Someone stays plump because they take no exercise.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Plump' looks like the adjective fat; it is the verb, as in 'plump for' something.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: to plump for one option is to choose it, with the 'for' dropped in crossword style.

entries.clue: One from that time who played Othello (4)

blocks.note: I is one in Roman numerals
ago = back in the past, from then

annotation.surface: An actor from the old days who once played Othello.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Played Othello' suggests an actor in the role; it means Iago played him for a fool.
annotation.definitionFit: Iago tricks and manipulates Othello in Shakespeare's play.

entries.clue: Reptiles associated with place of dead cat (13)

blocks.note: tortoises are reptiles
hell is a place for the dead

annotation.surface: A reptile keeper links the pet cat's death to one place.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dead cat' reads as a phrase, but 'cat' stands alone as the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A tortoiseshell is a cat with a mottled black and orange coat.
